newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate rises due to funds outflow.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate rises due to funds outflow.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to 7.9/8.0 percent on Thursday afternoon as the market tightened due to fresh outflow of funds, dealers said.

They said Wednesday's 500 million ringgit payment for a 30-day Bank Negara bill issue and intervention by Bank Negara in the foreign exchange market had tightened the market and pushed up the overnight rate.
Bank Negara on Wednesday is estimated to have sold $100-200 million to support the ringgit.
"The effect of the intervention should actually be felt tomorrow. Today, it is more psychological," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
Earlier, short-term interbank rates were slightly firmer due to fresh outflow of funds from the system, dealers said.
"The two factors of payment and intervention have combined to push up the short-end slightly, but the market is still flush," said a dealer with another Malaysian bank.
He said the market would tighten further next Wednesday, when Bank Negara issues one billion ringgit of Bank Negara bills against a maturity of only 500 million.

At the end of the morning session, one-week money was at 6.90 percent against 6.50/60 percent on Wednesday, two-week was at 7.00/10 percent against 6.70/80 percent and three-week at 7.20 percent against 7.15/20 percent.
One-month at 7.20/25 percent, three-month at 7.30/35 percent and six-month at 7.33/38 percent, were all unchanged.
